t.7.50.1: Thus urged by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, the charioteer began to relate the words that had been spoken by the sage.
t.7.50.2: Long ago, indeed, the great sage named Durvāsā, son of Atri, dwelt through the rainy season in the holy hermitage of Vasiṣṭha.
t.7.50.3: Your father, of great splendour and very great renown, went himself to that hermitage, desiring to see the great-souled family priest.
t.7.50.4: Seeing the great sage, resembling the sun and seeming to blaze with splendor, seated at the left side of Vasiṣṭha, he humbly saluted those two sages, the foremost of ascetics.
t.7.50.5: The king was honored by the two of them with words of welcome and a seat, with water for washing his feet, and with fruits and roots; and he, too, sat there together with the sages.
t.7.50.6: As those supreme sages sat there, many delightful conversations took place among them, when the sun had reached the middle of the day.
t.7.50.7: Then, in the course of some conversation, the king, with joined palms and in a humble manner, spoke to that great-souled son of Atri, rich in austerities.
t.7.50.8: O blessed one, of what extent will my lineage be? Of what span of life is my Rāma, and of what span of life are my other sons?
t.7.50.10: Having heard those words spoken by King Daśaratha, the greatly radiant Durvāsās began to speak.
t.7.50.9: And the sons that Rāma may have, how long will their life be? O blessed one, grant my wish and tell me the destiny of this lineage of mine.
t.7.50.11: Rāma will be the lord of Ayodhyā for a long time, and his younger brothers too will be happy and prosperous.
t.7.50.12: After a long time, it is said, the righteous-souled one will, for some reason, abandon both you and the illustrious Maithilī.
t.7.50.13: Having ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years and ten hundred years, Rāma will go to the world of Brahmā.
t.7.50.14: Having sacrificed with rich horse-sacrifices, Kākutstha, conqueror of enemy cities, will establish many royal dynasties.
t.7.50.15: Having related in full all the past and future of this king's dynasty, that one of very great energy and great splendor fell silent.
t.7.50.16: When that sage had fallen silent, King Daśaratha then saluted the two great-souled ones and returned once more to the finest of cities.
t.7.50.17: These words, spoken long ago by the sage, were heard by me there and laid up in my heart; it will not turn out otherwise.
t.7.50.18: Things having come to this, you should not give way to grief, Rāghava. For Sītā's sake or for Rāghava's sake, be firm, O best of men.
t.7.50.19: Having heard that most wondrous speech spoken by the charioteer, he attained incomparable delight and said, "Excellent, excellent!"
t.7.50.20: While the two, the charioteer and Lakṣmaṇa, were thus conversing on the road, the sun went to its setting; then the two took up their lodging and dwelt on the Gomatī.
